meta.title: The Data Grid for Trading and Financial Dashboards | AG Grid
meta.description: Build real-time trading and financial dashboards with AG Grid: high-frequency transaction updates, cell flashing, sparklines, aggregation and Excel export.

hero.heading: The data grid for trading and financial dashboards
hero.subHeading: Stream live prices into a grid that updates rows in place, highlights changes and keeps totals current, in React, Angular, Vue or JavaScript.

shortAnswer: AG Grid updates rows in place with transactions, batches high-frequency updates with applyTransactionAsync, flashes or animates cells when values change, and keeps grouping and aggregation current as data streams in. Transactions, async batching, row IDs and cell flashing are in the free AG Grid Community edition. Sparklines, aggregation, grouping, pivoting, cell range selection, clipboard, Excel export and the Server-Side Row Model are in AG Grid Enterprise.

capabilities.heading: Capabilities for trading and financial dashboards

items.title: High-frequency updates
items.body: applyTransactionAsync() queues transactions and applies them in one batch after a wait that defaults to 50ms; asyncTransactionWaitMillis changes the wait, flushAsyncTransactions() applies pending transactions immediately, and the asyncTransactionsFlushed event fires after each batch.

items.title: Row IDs
items.body: The getRowId grid option returns a unique, stable string ID per row. Transactions use it to match update and remove items by key; without it the grid compares object references, which the docs describe as slower for large data sets.

items.title: Cell change flashing
items.body: Column property enableCellChangeFlash=true flashes a cell when its value changes; the flashCells(params) API flashes chosen rows, columns or cells on demand. cellFlashDuration and cellFadeDuration set timing (defaults 500ms and 1,000ms via CSS classes ag-cell-data-changed and ag-cell-data-changed-animation).

items.title: Animated change renderers
items.body: Built-in cell renderers that show the difference between old and new value in green or red with a direction arrow, or slide and fade the previous value out.

items.title: Sparklines
items.body: Mini line, area, bar and column charts rendered inside grid cells from array data, configured through sparklineOptions. Requires SparklinesModule from ag-grid-enterprise plus an AG Charts module (Community or Enterprise).

items.title: Server-Side Row Model
items.body: Lazy-loads rows and group children from the server in blocks, with grouping, pivoting and aggregation delegated to the server. Supports applyServerSideTransaction and applyServerSideTransactionAsync (batched by asyncTransactionWaitMillis); SSRM transactions require row IDs.

items.title: Aggregation
items.body: aggFunc on a column (sum, min, max, count, avg, first, last, or a custom function) calculates group values; group and grand total rows are available. Transactions on grouped data recompute aggregations only for changed groups and their parents.

items.title: Pivoting
items.body: pivotMode with pivot columns generates pivot result columns from column values; at least one aggregation column is required. Configurable in column definitions, via the API, or by users through the Side Bar or Pivot Panel.

items.title: Cell range selection
items.body: cellSelection=true enables Excel-like selection of cell ranges by mouse drag, Shift+click and keyboard, used for highlighting, copying to the clipboard or showing aggregations in the Status Bar.

items.title: Excel export
items.body: Built-in .xlsx export from the context menu or the Grid API, with no third-party library. By default it exports the grid as rendered (column order, filters, sort, grouping) using value getters, and value formatters for text cells, but not cell renderers or cell styles. Number cells are exported as numbers.

howTo.heading: How to stream prices into AG Grid

steps.title: Give every row a stable ID
steps.body: Set `getRowId` so updates match existing rows by key, such as the ticker symbol.

steps.title: Send updates as transactions
steps.body: Call `api.applyTransactionAsync({ update })` from your WebSocket or message handler. The grid batches the updates and applies them together.

steps.title: Show what changed
steps.body: Set `enableCellChangeFlash` on price columns, or use `agAnimateShowChangeCellRenderer` to show the change in green or red.

steps.title: Format numbers for display
steps.body: Use a `valueFormatter` for currency. Formatted values are also used for copy and export.

howTo.outro: See the [finance dashboard demo](/example-finance/): live prices, sparklines, aggregation and Excel export in one grid.

faq.question: Can AG Grid handle real-time streaming updates?
faq.answer: Yes. AG Grid updates rows with transactions. applyTransactionAsync queues updates and applies them in one batch, by default every 50ms, which the AG Grid docs describe as more efficient for high-frequency data. It is included in AG Grid Community.

faq.question: How do I update row data in AG Grid?
faq.answer: Call api.applyTransaction or api.applyTransactionAsync with add, update and remove lists. Set getRowId so the grid matches updated rows by ID; without it the grid compares object references, which the docs describe as slower for large data sets.

faq.question: What does applyTransactionAsync do?
faq.answer: It queues a transaction and applies it together with any other queued transactions after a short wait, 50ms by default. asyncTransactionWaitMillis changes the wait and flushAsyncTransactions applies pending transactions immediately.

faq.question: How many rows can AG Grid handle?
faq.answer: AG Grid's row model guidance says the default Client-Side Row Model can handle 100k+ rows. For larger data sets, the Server-Side Row Model in AG Grid Enterprise loads rows from the server in blocks as users scroll.

faq.question: Does AG Grid support sparklines?
faq.answer: Yes. Sparklines render small line, area, bar and column charts inside grid cells. They are an AG Grid Enterprise feature.

faq.question: Can I use AG Grid for free?
faq.answer: Yes. AG Grid Community is free and open source under the MIT licence, including for commercial use. AG Grid Enterprise is a paid licence that adds features such as row grouping, pivoting, Excel export and the Server-Side Row Model.

proseClaims.claim: applyTransactionAsync() applies queued transactions together in one batch after 50ms by default, which the docs describe as more efficient.
asyncTransactionWaitMillis changes the wait between async transaction batches, flushAsyncTransactions() applies pending transactions immediately, and asyncTransactionsFlushed fires after each batch.
getRowId returns a string ID for each row that must always be the same for a given row and unique across rows.
Without row IDs, transactions match update and remove items by object reference, which is slower for large data sets.
Transactions on grouped data re-apply grouping, sorting, filtering and aggregation only to changed groups and their parents (Changed Path Selection).
enableCellChangeFlash=true on a column flashes cells when their values change, and flashCells(params) flashes chosen rows, columns or cells.
cellFlashDuration defaults to 500ms and cellFadeDuration to 1,000ms, applied through the CSS classes ag-cell-data-changed and ag-cell-data-changed-animation.
agAnimateShowChangeCellRenderer shows the change in green or red with a direction arrow; agAnimateSlideCellRenderer slides and fades the previous value out.
Sparklines are an Enterprise feature that render line, area, bar and column charts in cells, configured with sparklineOptions, and need SparklinesModule plus an AG Charts module.
The Server-Side Row Model is Enterprise, lazy-loads rows and group children in blocks, and delegates grouping, pivoting and aggregation to the server.
Server-side transactions require row IDs, and applyServerSideTransactionAsync batches transactions using asyncTransactionWaitMillis.
Aggregation is Enterprise; built-in aggFunc values are sum, min, max, count, avg, first and last, with custom functions and group and grand total rows available.
Pivoting is Enterprise, needs at least one aggregation column, and can be set in column definitions, through the API, or by users through the Side Bar or Pivot Panel.
Cell selection (Enterprise) is enabled with cellSelection=true and supports mouse drag, Shift+click and keyboard ranges for highlighting, clipboard copy and Status Bar aggregation.

Excel export (Enterprise) is built in with no third-party library, runs from the context menu or the Grid API, and by default uses value getters, and value formatters for text cells, but not cell renderers or cell styles.
The default Client-Side Row Model can handle 100k+ rows.
AG Grid Community is available under the MIT licence; Enterprise requires a commercial licence and adds features such as row grouping, pivoting, Excel export and the Server-Side Row Model.
Clipboard operations are an Enterprise feature; transactions, row IDs and cell flashing ship in AG Grid Community modules.
